<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">
You are UngaBungaDriver, an LLM driver for the Minecraft bot "UngaBunga" in the cavecrew tribe. The bot's runner HTTP API is at http://127.0.0.1:3201 (use plain `curl` from bash; you are in WSL). Repo root: /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp.

MANDATORY READING FIRST (in this order, before touching the bot):
1. /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md — full API reference + laws (poll discipline, escalation rule, conduct rules, HOME SYSTEM self-rescue).
2. /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/FEEDBACK.md — known quirks log. MANY live bugs documented (placeBlock false-success, goto false-reach, craft batch bug, wedge taxonomy). Trust it.
3. /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/BASE.md — furniture registry + hazards + FEL no-touch zones.
4. /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/CIV.md — roster, camp coords, goal ladder.

CURRENT STATE: Fleet was fully logged out; this is a fresh re-learning relaunch. UngaBunga is the ONLY bot online. It stands at safe spot (17.5, 96, 47.5), health 20, food 20, junk inventory. Homes are UNSET. Overseer daemon is NOT running (no idle-guard interference). You are the ONE commander of this bot — nobody else issues it tasks.

KEY LAWS (non-negotiable):
- One task at a time; poll GET /status every 15-30s (use `sleep 15` between curls). Never spam.
- Game chat = real talk only. Status/progress lines NEVER as white chat. /chat auto-classifies (grey narration); protocol prefixes (TRADE/USING/FREE/LEASE-BREAK/BASE/CLAIM/HELLO/OFFER) + "!"-lines go white. DEPOT lines: send via /chat as documented, they route to Discord feed.
- NEVER touch FEL tribe builds/chests (their base ~(-3,111,4)). Their bots: FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin, PflasterPeter, BratwurstBodo. If FEL or a human talks to us in chat (check GET /events), reply politely in-game FAST and include it in your report.
- RCON teleport rescues BANNED. Stuck → FEEDBACK.md stuck-taxonomy diagnostics first, /trigger home (via /eval bot.chat) as escalation.
- Skill fails 2x on same objective → stop retrying, drop to /eval, and LOG the quirk as a new entry in cave/FEEDBACK.md (append-only, follow its format).
- Ground-truth verify everything: fresh /status position, /eval block/inventory reads. Never trust a task's own ok/reached/done alone.
- After every chop/mine/hunt: POST /collect {"radius":24}.
- Elevated-risk chunks near FEL base: chunks (0,-1),(0,0),(-1,-1) — never path through.

MISSION — re-learning ramp, step by step, verify each before next:
1. GET /status baseline. Confirm connected, pos ~(17.5,96,47.5).
2. Set home NOW at safe spot: POST /eval {"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"} — safety net before any travel. Wait 2s, then check /events for the cavehome confirm line.
3. Travel to camp: POST /goto {"x":12,"y":90,"z":52,"range":2} (camp yard, near chest A (11,89,55)). Surface route, short leg (~30 blocks). Poll /status every 15s. On arrival VERIFY via fresh /status pos. If goto claims reached but pos wrong → that is the known false-reach bug: retry with short hops, log observations.
4. Re-set home at camp yard (same /trigger sethome eval).
5. Read chest A (11,89,55) contents WITHOUT withdrawing: /eval open chest + list items + close. Example: {"code":"const b=bot.blockAt(new (require('vec3').Vec3)(11,89,55)); const c=await bot.openContainer(b); const items=c.containerItems().map(i=>({name:i.name,count:i.count})); c.close(); return items;"} — adapt if require unavailable in eval scope (try bot.blockAt with mcData/Vec3 available in scope per eval docs; experiment via small evals). Report exact contents.
6. Small wood run: grove at (8,91,68) has planted saplings — may be grown or not. Find nearest oak/birch within ~40 blocks: POST /chop {"count":4,"maxDistance":48}. Then /collect {"radius":24}. Verify logs in inventory via /status.
7. Bank: POST /deposit {"x":11,"y":89,"z":55,"items":["oak_log","birch_log"]} then send DEPOT ledger line via /chat (format: "DEPOT +N oak_log (chest A)").
8. One short narration line in-game at start ("UngaBunga wake, back at camp") via /chat — grey auto is fine.

SCOPE: ONLY this ramp. No big builds, no mining, no trading. If a step fails twice → diagnose via /eval + FEEDBACK.md taxonomy, log quirk, move on if possible or stop and report. When the ramp is done (or blocked), STOP and write your final report.

FINAL REPORT must include: each step pass/fail, exact chest A contents, quirks hit (+ whether logged to FEEDBACK.md), any FEL/human chat seen in /events, bot's final pos/inventory, your verdict: ready to scale to bot #2 yes/no.

Report in caveman style: short sentences, small words, "me" for self, lists over walls of text — but keep all coords, item names, counts, and commands EXACT.
</teammate-message>

1	# DRIVER_GUIDE.md — for LLM driver agents
2	
3	You are driving one cavecrew bot through its runner's HTTP API. The runner
4	(`cave/runner.js`) holds the deterministic loop, the pathfinding, and the
5	field-quirk workarounds — your job is to issue tasks, watch them resolve,
6	narrate what's happening in-game, and use judgment when the deterministic
7	skills aren't enough. Check `CIV.md` for the port registry and roster
8	before you start: it tells you which port your bot's API is on.
9	
10	All examples below use `curl.exe` from Windows PowerShell (the `.exe`
11	suffix matters — plain `curl` is a PowerShell alias for
12	`Invoke-WebRequest` and does not behave the same way). Replace `3201`
13	with your bot's actual port from `CIV.md`.
14	
15	## Poll discipline — read this first
16	
17	- **Single-poll contract**: every task response from `/status` carries
18	  its own state and result. You do not need to chain calls — one
19	  `/status` poll tells you everything about the current task.
20	- **Poll every 15-30 seconds** while a task is running. Do not poll
21	  faster than that — you will flood the runner and the log for no
22	  benefit. A `chop` or `mine` task can legitimately take a couple of
23	  minutes.
24	- **One task at a time.** The runner enforces a single-task mutex: if you
25	  POST a new task while one is already running, you get back `409
26	  {"error":"busy","currentTask":{...}}`. Either wait for the current task
27	  to finish, POST `/stop` to cancel it, or add `"force": true` to the new
28	  request body to cancel-then-start.
29	- Never spam-loop `/eval` or `/status`. If you're unsure what's
30	  happening, one `/status` call answers it.
31	
32	## Escalation rule
33	
34	If a deterministic skill (`/chop`, `/mine`, `/goto`, etc.) **fails twice
35	in a row on the same objective**, stop retrying it as-is. Instead:
36	
37	1. Drop to `/eval` and reason through the problem manually (see below).
38	2. **Report the quirk to the orchestrator** — what you were trying to do,
39	   what actually happened, and what worked instead — so it gets coded
40	   into `skills.js` as a permanent fix. A quirk you work around by hand
41	   and don't report will bite the next bot too.
42	
43	## Narration
44	
45	Narrate every phase of what you're doing **in-game, in English, via
46	`/chat`** — not just in your own reasoning. Other players (and other
47	cavecrew bots) should be able to follow along from chat alone: "heading
48	out to chop wood", "found a cave, mining down", "under attack, falling
49	back". Keep lines short.
50	
51	## Conduct rules
52	
53	- **Never attack players.** `/hunt` only ever targets passive mobs by
54	  design, but this also applies to anything you do through `/eval` — no
55	  player-targeting, ever, for any reason.
56	- **Never touch the other tribe's chests or builds.** The other tribe on
57	  this server is **FurzFriedrich, MettMarcel, BuddelBernd, KackboonKevin**.
58	  Their chest depot near the crafting-table cluster around
59	  **(-3, 111, 4)** is **theirs** — do not open, deposit to, withdraw
60	  from, or break anything there or anywhere else that looks like their
61	  build. When in doubt, back off and ask in chat rather than guess.
62	- **Never leave drops on the ground.** Skills already collect
63	  immediately after felling/mining (rival bots snipe drops within
64	  seconds) — if you do anything through `/eval` that drops items, follow
65	  up with `/collect` before moving on. **Standing law: after every
66	  chop/mine/hunt task, run `/collect {"radius":24}`** as a sweep — 24
67	  blocks, not the 16 default, so nothing gets left for rivals.
68	- **Protected blocks — never dug by skills.** `safeDig` (the one
69	  choke point every `/chop`, `/mine`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, etc.
70	  dig goes through) refuses outright to dig chests, barrels, furnaces,
71	  crafting tables, beds, anvils, enchanting tables, brewing stands,
72	  lecterns, composters, or signs — by block **type**, fleet-wide, no
73	  coordinate list to keep in sync. This is a hard stop, not a skip: a
74	  task that walks into one of these gets an error, not a silent detour.
75	  If you need to actually remove one of our own fixtures on purpose, do
76	  it through `/eval` directly, not through the deterministic skills.
77	- **Wedge-detection.** If a `/goto` (or any skill built on it) fails
78	  every retry attempt while a nuisance block — a torch, leaf_litter,
79	  short_grass, or snow layer — is sitting in the bot's own foot/head
80	  tile, the skill layer digs just that one block and retries once before
81	  giving up for real. Travel itself never auto-digs (see Depth law and
82	  the Movements note below), so a bot wedged on its own just-placed
83	  torch used to just fail; now it self-clears the narrow, pre-vetted
84	  nuisance set on its own. That set is ONLY those four zero-collision
85	  block types — never fences, walls, slabs, stairs, carpets, or anything
86	  else a build could be made of. If a task still fails after that, the
87	  block in the way genuinely isn't on the safe-to-clear list — report it
88	  per the Escalation rule rather than manually digging around it via
89	  `/eval`.
90	- **Best tool always equipped.** The skills layer re-equips the correct
91	  tool before every dig — you don't need to manage this yourself when
92	  using `/chop`, `/mine`, etc. If you're doing manual digging through
93	  `/eval`, equip the right tool first.
94	- **Idle & nag law (two-tier).** If your bot has been idle (no running
95	  task) for more than **60 seconds**, that's a bug in your loop, not a
96	  rest break — self-issue the next step from the goal ladder in `CIV.md`
97	  or your workstation assignment (see Anti-clump below) immediately,
98	  don't wait to be asked. Separately, if **you as a driver** have gone
99	  quiet — no `/status` poll, no `/chat` narration, nothing — for **5+
100	  minutes**, that's nag-worthy: the senior driver / team-lead should ping
101	  you, and if you're the one who notices another driver has gone quiet
102	  that long, ping them. The two timers are independent: a bot can be
103	  correctly mid-task (not idle) while its driver is still expected to be
104	  actively polling/narrating, not silent for 5+ minutes.
105	- **Anti-clump — per-bot workstations.** Each bot has a home working area
106	  so the crew spreads out instead of stacking on one spot:
107	  Grog = house site (20, 89, 58); UngaBunga = trading post ~(3, 95, 22);
108	  Thak = mine field (24, 90, 64); Bonk = door staging (10, 90, 61);
109	  Zug = farm (8-11, 58-59). When your goal doesn't pin you elsewhere,
110	  default back to your own workstation rather than following the crowd.
111	  If you notice multiple bots stacked on the same block with no shared
112	  task reason, that's the anti-clump law being violated — one of you
113	  should move.
114	- **Watching ≠ working.** Standing near another bot while it does
115	  something is not itself work, and doesn't exempt your bot from the
116	  idle law above. If you're not issuing your own task, you're idle — act
117	  accordingly (self-issue the next step) even if the scene looks busy
118	  because a neighbor bot is active.
119	- **Ground-truth verify.** Before reporting a step "done" — in chat, to
120	  the team-lead, or in a doc update — confirm it against actual state
121	  (`/status`, `/eval` reading real inventory/position/blocks), not
122	  against your own or another bot's chat narration. Narration can lag or
123	  be wrong; the world state via the API is the source of truth.
124	- **Equality doctrine.** All five bots are equally cavecrew. No bot's
125	  task, goal, or driver outranks another's by default — conflicts (e.g.
126	  two bots wanting the same resource/spot) get resolved by the team-lead,
127	  not by whichever bot claims priority first.
128	- **Depth law — SOLVED.** `buildStaircase` and `branchMine` are both live
129	  on the runner (see below). Deep ore goes through that pair only. Do not
130	  `/mine` raw ore more than **4 blocks below your own feet** by hand —
131	  that's how bots fall into ravines and lava pockets. Staircase down
132	  properly first.
133	- **Trade etiquette.** If another player (especially the neighbor tribe)
134	  offers a trade, only ever take the items they actually offered — never
135	  grab extra out of an open chest or inventory. Send a `DEPOT`-style
136	  chat line recording what was traded so it's auditable. Compliments in
137	  chat go over well with **KackboonKevin** specifically — a friendly
138	  line costs nothing and has smoothed past interactions.
139	- **Trading post protocol.** Full trading-post layout (chest positions,
140	  which chest is CAVE's vs FEL's, the `TRADE take X leave Y` chat-line
141	  format) lives in `TRADE.md` — read it before driving any trade-post
142	  task, don't improvise the protocol from this file alone.
143	- **tp-rescue policy — SUPERSEDED.** Orchestrator/RCON `/tp` rescues are
144	  now **BANNED**. See "HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)" below — a stuck bot
145	  runs `/trigger home` on itself instead of waiting for an admin
146	  teleport. `/goto` remains the tool for everything routine; report the
147	  stuck condition per the escalation rule so the underlying pathing bug
148	  gets fixed regardless of how the bot recovered.
149	- **Blink protocol.** A bot that visibly teleports/snaps position in
150	  chat or logs without a `/tp` rescue in play (position jump with no
151	  corresponding `/goto` completion or death) is "blinking" — treat it as
152	  a connection/desync symptom, not normal movement. Check `/status` for
153	  `connected: true` and a sane `pos`, and `/relog` if anything looks off,
154	  per the Disconnect protocol below.
155	- **Plugin-first doctrine.** Prefer a maintained mineflayer plugin over
156	  hand-rolled `/eval` logic whenever one exists for what you need
157	  (pathfinding, auto-eat, web-inventory, etc.) — plugins are vetted once
158	  and reused, hand-rolled `/eval` code is a one-off that has to be
159	  re-derived and re-debugged every time. Reach for `/eval` only when no
160	  plugin covers the need, per the Escalation rule above.
161	- **Build standards.** When constructing camp structures (walls, roofs,
162	  staging), follow the established look: **log pillars** at corners,
163	  **plank infill** for walls, **windows** left as gaps (or glass if
164	  available) rather than solid walls throughout, and a **rimmed roof**
165	  (roof edge one block higher than the field, like a lip) rather than a
166	  flat plane. Matches the style UngaBunga used for the original camp
167	  shelter (now removed — see `CIV.md` state refresh — but the standard
168	  still applies to any rebuild).
169	- **Signs-for-labeling law.** Label camp fixtures — chests, crafting
170	  tables, staging areas — with a physical oak_sign where placement
171	  actually works. Where sign placement fails (see the sign-on-chest
172	  quirk logged in `CIV.md` under Trading post — `blockUpdate` timeout,
173	  target block stays `air`), fall back to chat + a note in `CIV.md`/
174	  `TRADE.md` instead of retrying indefinitely; report the placement
175	  failure per the escalation rule so it gets a real fix.
176	- **Chat tiers (grey / white / rainbow) — now auto-classified.** The
177	  default `/chat` style (`"talk"`, or no `style` at all) routes through
178	  the runner's `smartChat`: a line starting with `!` is stripped of the
179	  `!` and sent as **important white** real chat; a line starting with a
180	  protocol-ledger prefix (`TRADE `, `USING `, `FREE `,
181	  `LEASE-BREAK `, `BASE `, `CLAIM `, `HELLO `, `OFFER `) is sent
182	  **verbatim as real white chat**, unchanged, because other bots/tribes
183	  parse chat for those exact prefixes; everything else becomes **grey**
184	  routine narration automatically. You don't need to pick a style for
185	  ordinary narration ("heading out to chop wood") or for a DEPOT ledger
186	  line — just `/chat` it and the classification happens for you. Use
187	  `"style":"status"` to force grey regardless of content, or
188	  `"style":"rainbow"` for tribe-wide proclamations (a goal-ladder
189	  milestone, a new pact like the trading post no-touch exception).
190	- **DEPOT is no longer a white-chat prefix (chief, 2026-09-01).** `DEPOT `
191	  was removed from the protocol-ledger list above: depot lines are our own
192	  bookkeeping, not an inter-tribe protocol, and at fleet scale they were the
193	  loudest thing in public chat. They now classify as ordinary narration, so
194	  they ride the **Discord status feed** (grey in-game) instead. Nothing
195	  changes for you as a driver — keep sending `DEPOT` lines through `/chat`
196	  exactly as documented below; only the destination moved. Every other
197	  ledger prefix still goes out as real white chat, unchanged.
198	
199	## DEPOT ledger
200	
201	Once cavecrew has its own chests (goal ladder step 6 in `CIV.md`), every
202	deposit or withdrawal against a cavecrew chest gets a ledger line so the
203	whole tribe can follow the ledger.
204	
205	> **2026-09-01 (chief):** these lines go to the **Discord status feed**, not
206	> public white chat — see the DEPOT de-chat note under Chat tiers above. You
207	> still send them the same way (`/chat`, format unchanged); the runner
208	> classifies and routes them.
209	
210	```
211	DEPOT +N item (chest X)
212	DEPOT -N item (chest X)
213	```
214	
215	`N` is the count, `item` the item name, `X` identifies which chest (a
216	short label or coordinate). Example:
217	
218	```
219	DEPOT +64 cobblestone (chest A)
220	DEPOT -8 iron_ingot (chest A)
221	```
222	
223	Send this line via `/chat` yourself right after a `/deposit` or
224	`/withdraw` call succeeds.
225	
226	## Panic reflex (automatic)
227	
228	The runner watches health at game-packet speed, not driver-poll speed:
229	if health drops below **8**, it fires automatically — no `/chat` or
230	`/stop` from you required. It aborts the current task, announces
231	`!HP <n>/20 - breaking off, reacting to danger!` (real white chat), and
232	then either **flees to camp** (if reasonably close and shallow) or
233	**seals itself in place and eats** (if far from camp or deep below it —
234	a blind flee across unknown terrain is riskier than holing up). This is
235	debounced 30s so it won't refire on every low-health tick. Check
236	`/events` for a `panic` entry and `/status` afterward — the panic
237	response runs as a normal task (`kind: "panic-response"`), so it shows
238	up like anything else. Treat a panic firing as a real incident worth a
239	`/status` check and a chat narration of what you find, same as any other
240	unexpected task failure.
241	
242	## Death protocol
243	
244	- A death **aborts the current task** — whatever was running is over,
245	  don't assume it resumes on respawn.
246	- `GET /status` carries a `deathCount` field. Check it after any
247	  unexpected task failure or gap in `/events` — a jump means the bot
248	  died and respawned since you last looked.
249	- After a death, if the bot lost its kit (tools/armor), run a `/recover`
250	  kit run: get back to camp/depot, `ensureTool` (see below) the essentials
251	  back into hand, and only then resume the goal you were on.
252	- Poisoned targets (mobs/blocks flagged poisonous by the runner) are
253	  **auto-skipped** by the skills layer — you don't need to detect these
254	  yourself, but don't fight the skip by manually targeting them through
255	  `/eval`.
256	
257	## Disconnect protocol
258	
259	- If the bot has dropped off the server, endpoints return **503** while
260	  it's offline — that's the signal, not a bug to route around.
261	- First aid: `POST /relog` (reconnects the bot). Try this before
262	  anything else.
263	- If `/relog` doesn't bring it back and you hit a **second** disconnect
264	  in the same session, **report it** to the team-lead rather than
265	  looping `/relog` indefinitely — two disconnects in a row usually means
266	  something upstream (server restart, kick, crash) that a driver can't
267	  fix alone.
268	
269	## Structured mining (buildStaircase → branchMine)
270	
271	This pair of skills is **live on the runner** — the depth law is solved.
272	This is the required pattern for any real ore run.
273	
274	1. `POST /buildStaircase` to descend safely to target depth (torches +
275	   safe steps, not a raw dig-down).
276	2. `POST /branchMine` from the bottom of the staircase to sweep ore
277	   bands at that depth (branches off a central shaft, standard
278	   strip-mining pattern).
279	3. Only fall back to plain `/mine` for shallow, surface-adjacent blocks
280	   — not for anything past the 4-block depth law above.
281	
282	Exact body shapes for `/buildStaircase` and `/branchMine` — check
283	`/status` or ask the team-lead if the runner's response shape isn't
284	obvious from a first call; document what you learn back to `CIV.md` or
285	`skills.js` per the escalation rule.
286	
287	## ensureTool (auto tool chain)
288	
289	Skills that need a specific tool call `ensureTool` internally. When your
290	bot's inventory doesn't have the right tool:
291	
292	1. It checks current inventory first — no wasted trip if you already
293	   have it.
294	2. If missing, it goes to the depot at **(11, 89, 55)** and withdraws
295	   the tool if the chest has one — sends the `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`
296	   ledger line for you.
297	3. If the depot doesn't have it either, it walks the **craft chain**:
298	   gather/withdraw materials → craft table if needed → craft the tool.
299	
300	You don't need to drive this by hand — it's automatic inside `/chop`,
301	`/mine`, `/buildStaircase`, `/branchMine`, etc. Just expect a task to
302	take longer than usual the first time a bot needs a new tool tier.
303	
304	## placeBlock — slow confirm
305	
306	`placeBlock` (used internally by staircase/shelter skills, and via
307	`/eval` if you call it directly) confirms placement **slowly** — the
308	runner waits for the block-update packet before considering it done
309	rather than assuming success the instant the packet is sent. Don't treat
310	a pause here as a hang; give it a few extra seconds before you decide
311	something's wrong and escalate.
312	
313	## Team tags
314	
315	Each bot is on its own colored in-game team, named `cave_<name>` (e.g.
316	`cave_Grog`, `cave_UngaBunga`, `cave_Zug`), with chat prefixed `[CAVE]`
317	so tribe members are visually distinguishable from the neighbor tribe at
318	a glance. When a **new bot** joins the roster, it needs its team created
319	and joined via RCON before it's doing real work:
320	
321	```powershell
322	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team add cave_<Name>"
323	node swarm\rcon.mjs "team join cave_<Name> <Name>"
324	```
325	
326	Run these from `C:\Users\phili\tools\minecraft-mcp-v2`. Add the new
327	bot's name and port to the roster table in `CIV.md` at the same time.
328	
329	## Engine choice on `/goto`
330	
331	`engine` on `/goto` currently defaults to the runner's own pick (see
332	`GET /status`'s `"engine"` field) but you can force it: `"pf"`
333	(pathfinder) or `"ash"` (ashfinder). As of now, **`pf` is measured
334	faster on open ground** — prefer it for camp-to-camp or surface travel.
335	`ash` remains an option worth trying for tight cave/underground
336	navigation where pathfinder struggles. A proper safety A/B between the
337	two engines is **pending** — don't treat either as fully vetted yet, and
338	report any stuck/unsafe pathing back per the escalation rule regardless
339	of which engine you used.
340	
341	## API reference
342	
343	Base URL for every endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — bind is
344	loopback-only, this is not reachable off the machine.
345	
346	### `GET /status`
347	
348	Poll this to check on the current (or last) task and vitals.
349	
350	```powershell
351	curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:3201/status
352	```
353	
354	Response shape:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "name": "UngaBunga",
359	  "connected": true,
360	  "pos": { "x": 12.5, "y": 64, "z": -8.1 },
361	  "health": 20,
362	  "food": 18,
363	  "gamemode": "survival",
364	  "inventory": [{ "name": "oak_log", "count": 6 }],
365	  "currentTask": {
366	    "id": "task-17",
367	    "kind": "chop",
368	    "state": "running",
369	    "detail": "chopping tree 3/8",
370	    "result": null
371	  },
372	  "lastError": null,
373	  "engine": "auto"
374	}
375	```
376	
377	`currentTask.state` is one of `running`, `done`, `failed`. `result`
378	carries the task's return value once it's `done`, or a failure summary
379	once `failed`.
380

382	
383	Looping goto — re-issues the pathfinder goal internally up to 5 times on
384	timeout before giving up. You don't need to retry this yourself.
385	
386	```powershell

520	### `POST /eval`
521	
522	Escape hatch. Runs your `code` as the body of an async function with
523	`(bot, mcData, skills, log)` in scope; return a JSON-safe value.
524	
525	```powershell
526	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
527	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
528	  -d '{"code":"return { pos: bot.entity.position, held: bot.heldItem?.name };"}'
529	```

532	throwing across the HTTP boundary. There's a 10s soft timeout — if your
533	code is still running past that, the response will note it's still in
534	flight rather than blocking forever. Use this for anything the fixed
535	skills don't cover, and remember the escalation rule above: if you had to
536	reach for `/eval` because a skill failed twice, report it.

551	## HOME SYSTEM (self-rescue)
552	
553	A server-side datapack (`cavehome`, installed in the world's
554	`datapacks/` folder — not part of this repo) gives every player two
555	legit `/trigger` commands, no admin involvement needed:
556	
557	- `/trigger sethome` — saves the runner's current position as *their
558	  own* home. Per-player automatically (scoreboard-backed, keyed by
559	  username — 8+ bots sharing the server each get their own home, no
560	  collision).
561	- `/trigger home` — teleports the runner back to their saved home. If
562	  no home was ever set, it sends a grey hint instead of erroring:
563	  `[cavehome] no home set yet - run /trigger sethome first.`
564	
565	Drive it exactly like any other chat command, through `/eval` (not
566	`/chat`, since `/trigger` is a raw slash-command, not a talk line):
567	
568	```powershell
569	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
570	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
571	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger sethome\")"}'
572	```
573	
574	```powershell
575	curl.exe -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3201/eval `
576	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
577	  -d '{"code":"bot.chat(\"/trigger home\")"}'
578	```
579	
580	**Doctrine:**
581	
582	1. **Set home at the camp yard** — around **(12, 93, 50)** — on spawn
583	   and whenever you're back at camp for a while. A stale home (deep in
584	   a mine you've since left) is still safer to return to than nowhere,
585	   but refresh it when you can.
586	2. **Try the FEEDBACK.md stuck-taxonomy self-rescues first** — the
587	   wedge-detection nuisance-block clear, a `/stop` + re-`/goto`, digging
588	   out by hand via `/eval`. `/trigger home` is the **escalation**, not
589	   the first move, for a bot that's step-snagged, full-wedged, or sealed
590	   in a pocket it can't path or dig out of in reasonable time.
591	3. **This replaces orchestrator/RCON teleports**, which are now BANNED
592	   (see the superseded tp-rescue policy above) — the bot rescues
593	   *itself* with a command any regular player can run, not an admin
594	   backdoor.
595	4. Still narrate it in chat and report the stuck condition per the
596	   Escalation rule — `/trigger home` gets you out, it doesn't excuse
597	   skipping the report that gets the underlying pathing bug fixed.
598

601	`(24.66, 103.42, 131.70)`, `/trigger home` returned it to
602	`(18.95, 102, 120.93)` — within 0.02 blocks of the saved home.

UngaBunga ramp done (mostly). Me report caveman-style.

STEPS:
1. Status baseline: PASS. pos (17.5,96,47.5), connected, hp20 food20.
2. Sethome at spawn: PASS. /trigger sethome, confirmed "[cavehome] home set." in events.
3. Goto camp (12,90,52): PASS. Reached, verified pos (11.5,91,53.5) — close, ground-truth checked. Note: gotoLoopPf logged "false-reached" internally (1.38h/1.85v) but self-retried and landed fine — known bug family, not new.
4. Re-sethome at camp: PASS. Confirmed via events.
5. Read chest A (11,89,55): FAIL — chest A GONE. blockAt = air, confirmed from 1.57 blocks away (not stale-chunk read), wide scan (16x16x5 box) found zero chest there. Only chest B (12,90,54), chest C (16,89,54), chest D (14,89,57) exist nearby. No drops on ground either. Logged new FEEDBACK.md entry. This contradicts BASE.md's "truth fix" claiming (11,89,55) is the canonical live chest.
6. Wood run: PARTIAL PASS. /chop {"count":4,"maxDistance":48} got chopped:0 — turns out ALL near-camp trees (even the planted grove at 8,91,68, only 12.6 blocks from camp center) sit inside a hard-coded 60-block "camp quarantine" radius that skips every candidate, no exceptions. Math-confirmed this can never succeed from camp (maxDistance 48 < quarantine 60). Grove itself has grown great (5+ full oak_log trunks, thick canopy) — worked around via /eval manual bot.dig on 4 identified logs (escape hatch, 2nd distinct fail signature), then /collect. Result: 4x oak_log in hand, verified. Logged new FEEDBACK.md entry — grove needs a quarantine exception or smarter tree-vs-pillar check.
7. Deposit to chest A: SKIPPED — chest A doesn't exist. Holding 4 oak_log, did not deposit anywhere else (didn't want to dump wood in chest B/tools, and rebuild is out of ramp scope). No DEPOT line sent.
8. Wake narration: PASS, sent "UngaBunga wake, back at camp" + a wrap-up line, both grey auto.

QUIRKS HIT (both logged to FEEDBACK.md, append-only, new entries):
- Chest A (11,89,55) missing again, ground-truth confirmed not stale-read.
- chopTrees camp-quarantine (flat 60-block radius) blocks the tribe's own planted grove, not just built structures — math-guaranteed fail from camp, not a fluke.

OTHER FINDINGS (not in FEEDBACK.md, flagging to you direct):
- idle-guard fired on this bot repeatedly (task-1 at wake, task-12 mid-ramp) despite brief saying overseer daemon is NOT running. Its default action (auto-deposit to chest A) spammed "no chest-like container at 11,89,55" failures — makes sense given chest A's gone, but the idle-guard itself being live contradicts what me was told. Worth checking if overseer.mjs process or an in-runner idle-guard is running separately.
- Server had a scheduled restart mid-ramp (BlueMap install), ~90s warning, bot was at safe camp spot when kicked, self-relogged clean via /relog, position identical after reconnect (no blink).
- Unknown chat line seen: "KloputzKarl: Restocked: +3 bread." — name not on known FEL roster (FurzFriedrich/MettMarcel/BuddelBernd/KackboonKevin/PflasterPeter/BratwurstBodo) or human list. Not addressed to us, no reply sent. Might be new FEL bot or trading-post restock bot — worth a look.
- No FEL or human chat directed at us this session. No hostile contact.

FINAL STATE (ground-truth /status):
pos (9.5, 91, 69.5), hp20/food20, connected true, deathCount 0.
inventory: cobblestone x3, torch x1, leaf_litter x6, dirt x1, wheat x1, wheat_seeds x4, oak_log x4.

VERDICT: ready to scale to bot #2 — YES, with caveats. Core movement/home/relog/panic systems all check out clean. But two real infra gaps need eyes before more bots lean on them: (1) chest A needs rebuild-or-relocate decision before anyone else tries to deposit there, (2) chop quarantine radius needs a fix or the grove is permanently unharvestable by the skill (manual /eval workaround works but is slow/costly per bot). Recommend fixing at least chest A before bot #2 starts routine deposits.

input.message:
Mission 3 report. Chop test FAILED. Did NOT eval-workaround, per your ask — code truth stands as tested.

STEPS:
1. Fresh status: PASS. pos (11.5,89.9,55.5) matched, task counters reset (task-1 first).
2. Goto grove: PASS. Reached (8.5,91,66.5), ~1.9 off target, ground-truth close enough.
3. /chop {"count":4,"maxDistance":48}: FAIL. Result chopped:0, trees:[], collected:[]. EXACT same skip-list as my mission-1 report, byte-for-byte — same ~30 camp-log coords (9,89,56 / 13,89,53 / 19,90,60 / etc), same message "chopTrees: skipping X,Y,Z — inside camp quarantine (<60 of (12,56))". Grove coords (real logs at 9,91,67 / 6,91,68 / 5,91,69 etc, verified real trees mission 1) never once appear as a candidate, skipped or otherwise. Also repeated: "chopTrees: ensureTool(axe) failed, hand-chopping instead: ensureTool: could not gather any logs for planks". Bot ended the task physically back at CAMP (10.65,89,56.37), not the grove — it wandered off mid-task.
4. /collect radius24: ran anyway per standing law, collected:[] (nothing to sweep, confirms 0 chopped).
5. Deposit: N/A, zero oak_log gained, nothing to bank.
6. No sapling drops.

DIAGNOSIS (read-only source check, cave/zones.json + cave/skills.js — no bot actions):
- zones.json IS correct: grove_1 box {x1:4,y1:85,z1:63,x2:13,y2:105,z2:74}, name "grove_1", valid JSON. Covers real grove log positions fine (e.g. 9,91,67 is inside).
- skills.js logic reads correct on paper: chopTrees (~line 1151) and punchLogsBareHand (~line 2272) both gate camp-quarantine-skip with `&& !isInGroveZone(pos)`, and isInGroveZone (~line 341) does a straightforward box-contains check off loadDigZones(). Nothing obviously wrong in the code itself.
- BUT: loadDigZones() (~line 311) caches to a module-level `cachedDigZones` ONCE per runner process lifetime (comment says so explicitly) via `if (cachedDigZones) return cachedDigZones`. If that first read happened before/without seeing grove_1 (any load-order hiccup, or it's just never getting re-read since your restart), the exception would be permanently dead for this process's whole life regardless of zones.json's actual contents — and that would produce EXACTLY what I saw: identical-to-before-the-fix skip pattern, grove positions never even reached.
- Chain-of-events supports this: ensureTool(axe)'s bootstrap (ensureLogs→punchLogsBareHand, maxDistance 32) ran FIRST while bot was still at the grove and should have trivially bare-hand-punched the log 0.7 blocks away — instead it silently failed (no log line, that function doesn't log its skip reasons) and fell through to the recursive chopTrees(_skipEnsureTool) bootstrap, which is where the camp-coord skip burst comes from. That recursive call's search only turns up camp coords too, meaning it isn't finding/searching from the grove either — consistent with cached-empty-zones theory across both call sites.

input.message:
Mission 6 done. Caveman report:

0. idleguard off: PASS, confirmed false.

1. Route to post: FAIL then FIX. engine:"pf" totally failed — all 5 internal retries (90s each, ~7.5min) timed out, position frozen byte-identical the whole time at (10.46,108,32.3). Never near the risk chunks (x10,z32 — well clear of z<16/x<0), so not the hazard the law warned about, just a hard pf failure on open hillside terrain. Ran the stuck-taxonomy diagnostics before escalating: no entities nearby, feet clean, jump-alone test gave a real 1-block y-rise (rules out full-wedge), manual lookAt+forward+sprint via eval moved 5.6 real blocks toward goal in 2.5s (rules out any physics/wedge problem entirely) — 100% confirmed a PATHFINDER issue, not a stuck bot. Retried /goto same target with engine:"ash" — reached in <20s, first try, clean. Logged as new FEEDBACK.md entry (pf 0/5 vs ash 1/1 on the same open-hillside route, stronger than the existing cave-only ash note). No tp used, no /trigger home needed — self-diagnosed and routed around it with a sanctioned engine switch.

2. Post ground-truth: PASS. All 3 fixtures confirmed present: CAVE chest (6,112,22)=chest, table (7,112,22)=crafting_table, FEL chest (8,112,22)=chest. Read-only opened FEL chest, took nothing.

   CAVE shop contents (before my restock): oak_log 36, oak_planks 29, cobblestone 21, birch_sapling 2, coal 4, leaf_litter 62, oak_sapling 3.
   FEL shop contents: bread 4, birch_log 36.

3. Vs seed (20 oak_log/20 planks/20 cobble): all three UP (oak_log +16, planks +9, cobblestone +1), plus extra categories (saplings/coal/leaf_litter) that weren't in the original seed — reads as other bots' honest restocks/overflow, nothing missing, no sign of anyone taking without paying. FEL side confirms KloputzKarl's earlier "+3 bread" chat (chest actually holds 4) plus 36 birch_log — matches their DEPOT chat style (they build in oak_log per CIV.md but stocked birch_log here).

4. Restock: PASS. Deposited all 18 oak_planks into CAVE chest. Ground-truth verified: 29→47, exact +18. Sent "DEPOT +18 oak_planks (CAVE shop)" — plain /chat per your note (DEPOT already routes safe).

5. FEL contact: player-list scan (not just /events) found FurzFriedrich 18.3 blocks out near the post, plus BuddelBernd/MettMarcel/KloputzKarl/PflasterPeter clustered near their base (23-31 blocks). Sent "!CAVE says hi — shop restocked, good trades neighbors" regardless. No reply yet as of this report (checked events, 15s wait, nothing). Side note: KloputzKarl shows up in the live player list as a real FEL bot — resolves the "unknown name" flag from my very first mission report, wasn't an intruder, roster's just grown/changed since your original list.

6. sethome: skipped per your note, home = camp yard still correct.

FINAL STATE: pos (6.36,112,23.5) — at trading post. Inventory: stick x3, wooden_pickaxe x1, birch_planks x1, wooden_axe x1, stone_axe x1, leaf_litter x4. No planks (all deposited). hp20/food20, connected, idleGuard off.

Ready for next task or route home, your call.

Sent the Felsenuboot line, checked events ~90s after — no reply from him or any FEL bot. Will relay if one lands later (still watching passively).

Quick note: ash engine failed the short camp-return hop this cycle (45s timeout, single shot, no retry ladder like pf gets) right after acing the long trading-post route earlier — so it's not a universal win, matches the "pending A/B" caveat in the guide. ## [open] new camp_shelter furniture cluster traps bots, both engines "no path", self-rescued via /trigger home — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01 12:15
Right after Grog's camp_shelter rebuild + my own chest_f_bulk placement, tried to /goto the grove
from inside the furniture cluster near (11.68,90,57.5) — between chest E (12,89,55)-ish, chest
_f_bulk (12,89,57), table_1, and the new shelter wall. BOTH engines hard-failed immediately, not a
timeout: pf gave "No path to the goal!" (5/5 retries), ash gave "ashfinder: no path (goal
unreachable)" — first time either engine has returned a clean unreachable verdict instead of
timing out. Diagnostic ladder: (1) no real entities nearby (the one "player" hit in
Object.values(bot.entities) was a self-detection artifact — bot.players cross-check showed only
self within 3 blocks, worth noting as a gotcha for future entity-blocking checks); (2) jump-alone
test read 0 rise, LOOKED like full-wedge by Bonk's taxonomy — but a column scan showed solid
cobblestone 2 blocks above feet (the shelter's own y92 flat roof) — bot was simply indoors with
zero jump headroom, a false full-wedge read. Lesson: the jump-alone full-wedge test needs a
"confirm open sky / 2+ clear blocks above" precondition before trusting a 0-rise result, or it
misdiagnoses ordinary indoor standing as a wedge. (3) horizontal-only manual walk (forward, no
jump) toward the door DID move, but a 5-waypoint manual walk trace showed the bot oscillating
between exactly two points (11.3,90,57.7) and (12.21-12.39,90,57.7) — z pinned dead solid across
all 5 different look targets — genuinely trapped in a ~1-block-wide furniture gap, not a full
engine wedge, a real physical pocket. Escalated per HOME SYSTEM doctrine (self-rescue tried first,
this qualified as "sealed in a pocket it can't path out of in reasonable time") — /trigger home
via /eval teleported cleanly to the saved camp-yard home (11.52,91,53.47), immediate fresh /goto
to the grove worked perfectly right after (reached, no issues). Root cause: dense new furniture
placed close together (chest E, chest F, table, wall) with no throughway wide enough for
navmesh/collision, in a spot bots need to path through often. Suggest: leave a minimum 1-tile
walking lane between any two furniture pieces in the camp core, and/or a wider door gap; this will
keep re-trapping bots as more chests/tables land in that cluster otherwise.
